solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Description of study — presumably one well-panelled

definitions.text: Description of study — presumably one well-panelled

parts.words: Description of study — presumably one well-panelled
parts.note: a '... study' is a reverie, and the clue pretends the phrase comes from a room lined with dark wood panelling

explanation.surface: A guess at why a certain kind of study got its name: the walls were panelled in wood.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'brown study' is an idiom for being lost in thought; the clue pretends the colour comes from a study (the room) lined with dark wooden panels.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a brown study' means a fit of absent-minded musing, so the colour word describes that kind of study.

clue.text: Friend, say, picked up shift

parts.note: bud is informal for a friend or mate

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means the letters for 'say' are lifted so they read bottom to top

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated e.g.

explanation.surface: A friend, perhaps, collected someone after their work shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like collecting someone, but in a down entry it means the abbreviation for 'say' is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To shift something is to move it slightly, a synonym of the verb meaning to move or give way.

clue.text: Ape sounded alarm, having released one outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for released sits around the word for sounded alarm

parts.note: released means let out
rang, as a bell sounding the alarm
an is the article meaning one

explanation.surface: An ape raised the alarm after letting someone out of its enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Released' wants to be a verb in the story; it is the word for let out, split open by the bell-ringing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The orang-utan is a great ape of Borneo and Sumatra, so it is an example of an ape.

clue.text: Nothing less than single expression of relief shown by relative

indicators.note: Nothing less than single is read as the word for single minus the zero

parts.note: single means one
O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
phew is what one says when relieved

explanation.surface: A relative sighed with relief at nothing less than being single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing less than single' reads as an emphatic phrase, but it means ONE with O (nothing) removed, leaving NE.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's son is a family member, so he is an example of a relative.

clue.text: Irish sailors having access to bottle

parts.note: Cork's, belonging to the Irish city and county of Cork
a crew is a ship's company of sailors

explanation.surface: Some Irish sailors have a way of getting at the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cork is a city and county in Ireland, so its sailors are Cork's crew; the possessive apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral tool for drawing corks is what lets you open, and so get into, a wine bottle.

clue.text: Abandon a lake — here's narrower artificial waterway

parts.note: to can a plan is to scrap or abandon it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Give up on the lake: this man-made channel is narrower.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition may mislead: 'narrower' contrasts the man-made channel with a river, many such channels being built for narrow boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made channel for boats is typically slimmer than a river, so the phrase describes one fairly.

clue.text: Borrow novel, French novel, taking year with the antique style

parts.note: roman is the French word for a novel
ye is an old-fashioned spelling of the, as in Ye Olde Shoppe

explanation.surface: Borrowing a French novel, taking a year over it, in an old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Borrow' is not a verb here: George Borrow was a 19th-century English writer of books about Gypsy life, and this is one of his novels.
explanation.definitionFit: George Borrow's 1857 sequel to Lavengro bears this title, so it is a novel by Borrow.

clue.text: Loose rocks landing on church producing alarmed sound

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece landing on another sits above it

parts.note: scree is loose stones on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: Rocks tumbling down onto a church make people cry out in fright.
explanation.definitionFit: A screech is a harsh shrill cry, the kind of noise made by someone frightened.

clue.text: Only some aware Germany boasts this composer

indicators.note: Only some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Few people know that Germany can claim this composer as its own.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'boasts this composer' as definition, but 'boasts' cannot stand for a composer's name; it is a link in the surface, leaving 'this composer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Reger was a German composer and organist active around 1900, famed for organ works.

clue.text: Comedian, stressed about hospital, pulled out

indicators.note: about says the comedian and stressed words go round the hospital letter

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
drawn means looking strained and tense

explanation.surface: A tense comedian, worried about a hospital visit, pulled out of the gig.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops withdrawn from a place have been taken away from it, the same sense as pulled out.

clue.text: Notice power's seized by university official without emotion

indicators.note: seized by says the notice and power letters are held inside the official's title

parts.note: a dean heads a faculty or college
ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A university official coldly takes control of a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadpan face or delivery shows no feeling at all, which is what lacking emotion means.

clue.text: Bishop in power? The man that's wanted

indicators.note: in says the bishop's letters go inside the word for power

parts.note: might means power or strength
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop holding power is the man everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the ideal partner someone is waiting to meet, the one person desired.

clue.text: Dog losing head in good hole

indicators.note: losing head says the dog's first letter goes

parts.note: a beagle is a breed of hound

explanation.surface: A dog lost its head down a good hole in the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In golf a hole played in two under par is a fine score, so 'good hole' is fair.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf, two strokes under par on a single hole is a very good result with this bird's name.

clue.text: Student, working with engine parts, provided with enhanced auditory capacity?

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
on means functioning, working
geared means fitted with gears, parts of an engine

explanation.surface: A student mechanic tinkering with engines has been given better hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: big ears are imagined as giving better hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Having big ears, like a hare or bat, is imagined as giving keener hearing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Heads balls

definitions.meaning: nut is slang for the head, so heads are this in the plural
slang for testicles, and also an exclamation meaning nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang both for heads, as in 'off your nut', and for testicles.

clue.text: Quantity of claret thwarting assessment of bouquet?

definitions.text: Quantity of claret thwarting assessment of bouquet?

parts.words: Quantity of claret thwarting assessment of bouquet?
parts.note: claret is old slang for blood, and blood streaming from the nostrils would spoil anyone's sniffing of a wine's aroma

explanation.surface: Some red wine spoils the judging of its aroma at a tasting.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine-tasting picture misleads: claret is slang for blood, and the bouquet is judged with the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood running from the nose would stop a taster smelling a wine, and claret is slang for blood.

clue.text: Solid figures upset that reader

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some solid shapes have upset that reader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges THAT READER.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-faced solids with triangular faces are geometric shapes in three dimensions, here in plural.

clue.text: Unexpected deal with China to produce Mexican food

indicators.note: an unexpected arrangement signals that the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A surprising trade deal with China results in Mexican cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unexpected' rearranges DEAL and CHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled tortilla with filling and chilli sauce is a classic dish of Mexico.

clue.text: Fatal assault delivered by the bad criminal (mean)

indicators.note: criminal suggests something crooked, so these letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: low means mean or base

explanation.surface: A deadly attack carried out by a nasty, petty criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges THE BAD into DEATHB; the bracketed 'mean' adds LOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A final blow that kills is a lethal attack, in literal or figurative use.

clue.text: Food dished up for swish dance

indicators.note: dished up suggests something served out in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food is served for a smart dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dished up' looks like serving the food, but it rearranges SWISH DANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread slices with a filling are a common kind of food, especially at buffets.

clue.text: State political group receiving half of your money

indicators.note: receiving says the faction's word takes the other pieces into it

parts.note: a wing is a faction of a political party

indicators.note: half of says take only the first two letters of the four-letter word your

explanation.surface: A political faction takes in half of your cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half of' keeps the first two letters of 'your'; 'receiving' places them, with the money letter, just after the first letter of the faction word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the mountain West.

clue.text: Farm location that's well down the pub crawl

parts.note: each stop on a pub crawl is a bar
N stands for an indefinitely large number, so 'well down' the list is the nth stop

explanation.surface: Somewhere on a farm is reached after many stops on a drinking tour.
explanation.walkthrough: Number the stops of a pub crawl bar A, bar B and so on; bar N is well down the list.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm building for storing hay, grain or animals is a place found on farms.

clue.text: Irresolute about everything, one keeps notes

indicators.note: about says the feeble word goes round the word for everything

parts.note: wet means feeble or irresolute
all means everything

explanation.surface: A dithering person is unsure about everything and keeps written notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One keeps notes' sounds like a person with a notebook; here the notes are banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small folding case carries banknotes, so it is something that holds notes.

clue.text: Tunnelling due to appear after rough sound

indicators.note: after says the word for due comes behind the rough sound

parts.note: a burr is a rough rolled pronunciation of R or a whirring noise
owing means due to be paid

explanation.surface: Digging is set to begin after a grinding noise is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals such as rabbits dig holes and passages, which is tunnelling underground.

clue.text: Degenerates will embrace love at bottom

indicators.note: will embrace says the decay word holds the love letter inside

parts.note: rots means decays or degenerates
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: Wicked people will embrace love at their lowest point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerates' looks like a noun for wicked people; it is the verb, ROTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The roots of something are its base or source, what is at the bottom of it.

clue.text: It's some dancing, I guess

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone offers a hesitant guess that a performance counts as dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a description: a lively Baroque dance is indeed some dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue word points at the thing itself, a lively Baroque dance in compound time.

clue.text: Thomas following a famous swordsman

indicators.note: following says the name comes after the A

parts.note: Thos is the old abbreviation for the name Thomas

explanation.surface: Thomas trails behind a celebrated fencer.
explanation.walkthrough: Athos is one of Dumas's Three Musketeers.
explanation.definitionFit: One of Dumas's Three Musketeers, he is a celebrated literary swordsman.

clue.text: Not like tropical weather currently in Seychelles

indicators.note: in says the word for currently goes inside the country code

parts.note: SY is the international vehicle code for the Seychelles
now means at present

explanation.surface: The weather in the Seychelles is not tropical at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: SY is the international code for the Seychelles, the Indian Ocean islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with falling flakes is cold and wintry, the opposite of tropical heat.

clue.text: What's excellent about sex or perverse sexual material?

indicators.note: perverse means turned the wrong way, so the assembled letters read backwards
about says the excellent word goes round the sex word and 'or'

parts.note: ace means excellent
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A question of whether something about sex is wonderful or kinky material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts the excellent word round the sex word and 'or', giving ACITORE; 'perverse' then turns the whole thing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing or images meant to arouse are material of a sexual kind, often in book or film form.

clue.text: Astronomer's endless success penning line on constellation

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', so the definition is the astronomer

indicators.note: on says the constellation follows in the across entry
penning says the shortened word encloses the line letter
endless says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a gain is a success or win
Leo, the Lion, is a zodiac constellation

explanation.surface: An astronomer's unfinished triumph involves drawing a line across a constellation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts GAIN to GAI; 'penning' puts L inside it to make GALI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian scientist who first turned a telescope on Jupiter's moons was a pioneering stargazer.

clue.text: Expected to succeed, agents die in calamity

indicators.note: in calamity suggests things thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Secret agents perish in a disaster, as anticipated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In calamity' rearranges AGENTS DIE.
explanation.definitionFit: After a title, as in 'president designate', the word marks someone chosen but not yet in office.

clue.text: Description of port: Welsh name, but in Scottish river

indicators.note: in says the two abbreviations go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A port wine is described with a Welsh name, though found in a Scottish river.
explanation.walkthrough: Port here is the fortified wine; one aged in wood is described by its brownish colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A port aged in wooden casks turns a brownish-amber colour and is labelled by that colour term.
